what_its_for: Nelfinavir is an antiviral medicine used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) infection. It belongs to a group of medicines called 'protease inhibitors.' It works by blocking a protein that HIV needs to make copies of itself, which helps lower the amount of HIV in your body and keeps your immune system stronger. It is always used together with other HIV medicines, never alone.
how_to_take: Take nelfinavir by mouth with a meal or light snack — food is very important because it helps your body absorb the medicine much better. Swallow the tablets whole, or you may crush them and mix them with a small amount of water, milk, formula, soy milk, or dietary supplements. Do not mix crushed tablets with acidic foods or juice (like orange juice or applesauce) because this makes the medicine taste very bitter. Take this medicine exactly as your doctor prescribed and do not skip doses, as this can make the HIV virus harder to treat.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 1,250 mg (five 250 mg tablets) taken twice a day with food, OR 750 mg (three 250 mg tablets) taken three times a day with food. For children (2 to 13 years old), the dose is based on body weight and is usually given three times a day with food. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to take. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is not almost time for your next dose. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Try to take your medicine at the same times every day to help you remember.
storage: Store nelfinavir tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Do not take nelfinavir with certain medicines because dangerous interactions can occur. These include: rifampin (an antibiotic), St. John's Wort (a herbal supplement), certain cholesterol medicines like simvastatin or lovastatin, some sedatives like triazolam or oral midazolam, and the ergot medicines used for migraines. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, herbs, and supplements you take before starting nelfinavir. Avoid missing doses, as this makes it easier for HIV to become resistant to the medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not stop; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); increased thirst or urination, blurred vision, or unexplained weight loss (signs of high blood sugar); unusual bleeding or bruising; muscle pain or weakness; a rash or allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat; or any new or worsening symptoms. Also call if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Nelfinavir does not cure HIV, but it starts working right away to lower the virus level in your blood. You may not feel different at first, but blood tests (called viral load and CD4 counts) will show your doctor how well the medicine is working over time. It usually takes several weeks to months to see significant improvement in lab results. It is very important to keep taking your medicine every day, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Nelfinavir can be used during pregnancy, but your doctor needs to carefully monitor you and your baby. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking nelfinavir because HIV can be passed to your baby through breast milk. Children: Nelfinavir can be used in children 2 years of age and older. The tablets can be crushed and dissolved in liquid to make it easier for children to take. Kidney or Liver Problems: Tell your doctor if you have any liver or kidney disease, as this may affect how your body processes the medicine. Diabetes: Nelfinavir may raise your blood sugar levels, so let your doctor know if you have diabetes or notice symptoms of high blood sugar.
